mkp-math:plane@1.name: plane
mkp-math:plane@1.about: A coordinate plane in a frame: a light grid, numbered axes and their names, and on it functions, curves, points, segments, shaded regions and heat, with up to four parameters in the bar that every expression can use.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: the frame's title

inputs.name: caption
inputs.about: what kind of figure it is, said small before the title (Plot, Fit, Simulation, Coverage)

inputs.name: xmin
inputs.about: left edge

inputs.name: xmax
inputs.about: right edge

inputs.name: ymin
inputs.about: bottom edge

inputs.name: ymax
inputs.about: top edge

inputs.name: kind
inputs.about: complex names the axes Re and Im and marks the imaginary ticks with i

inputs.name: step
inputs.about: grid spacing; 0 picks one, about nine lines across

inputs.name: numbers
inputs.about: number the ticks

inputs.name: xlabel
inputs.about: the x axis's name, words or maths; empty: x (Re on the complex plane)

inputs.name: ylabel
inputs.about: the y axis's name; empty: y (Im)

inputs.name: aspect
inputs.about: width over height; 0 takes the ranges' own, kept between 1.6 and 2.8

inputs.name: equal
inputs.about: one unit as long on both axes: the shorter way is widened about its middle to fill the aspect

inputs.name: size
inputs.about: kept for older documents: the plane fills its frame

inputs.name: label
inputs.about: what the plane shows, for screen readers

inputs.name: params
inputs.about: up to four knobs, called a, b, c and d in the expressions below, in this order; the name is maths (\theta); one or two sit in the bar, three or four in a Parameters popover

inputs.name: functions
inputs.about: y = f(x) across the view

inputs.name: curves
inputs.about: parametric curves, t running from from to to

inputs.name: points
inputs.about: points that follow the parameters, each named in a chip beside it

inputs.name: dots
inputs.about: fixed points to mark

inputs.name: segments
inputs.about: segments between fixed points

inputs.name: regions
inputs.about: shaded where f(x, y) < 0 and outlined, the label at at (else in the middle)

inputs.name: heats
inputs.about: f(x, y) as shading: faint at lo, strong at hi (both 0: the lowest and highest values in view)

inputs.name: cells
inputs.about: cells along the longer side, for regions and heat

inputs.name: status
inputs.about: the bar's line, in parts joined by a dot: each a text, the value of f (when given) and a text after it

values.name: np
comment: the parameters: one var each, so a slider anywhere sets it

value.expr: map(range(0, 3), k => at(params, k, {name: "", label: "", min: 0, max: 1, step: 0, value: 0}))

values.name: xs
comment: the view: the ranges, widened to the aspect when units are equal

value.expr: if(equal and wider, (xmin + xmax)/2 - ys asp/2, xmin)
if(equal and wider, (xmin + xmax)/2 + ys asp/2, xmax)
if(equal and not wider, (ymin + ymax)/2 - xs/asp/2, ymin)
if(equal and not wider, (ymin + ymax)/2 + xs/asp/2, ymax)

values.name: px
comment: a pixel, about, each way (a lesson column is some 720 wide)

value.expr: if(step > 0, step, if(equal, xstep, nice(vy1 - vy0, max(3, round(12/asp)))))

values.name: hasx

values.name: yleft

values.name: cd

values.name: hb

map(range(0, len(heats) - 1), k => if(heats[k].lo == 0 and heats[k].hi == 0, {lo: min(map(hv[k], r => min(r))), hi: max(map(hv[k], r => max(r)))}, {lo: heats[k].lo, hi: heats[k].hi}))
